title: Crucible Data Quality Report
description: Exactly one data_quality.json per output directory. This artifact answers a single question: what did Crucible refuse to believe, and why. A pipeline that silently coerces bad input into plausible output is worse than one that crashes, because it launders a defect into a result. Every input record that was altered, quarantined, or partially trusted MUST be accounted for here.

records_modified.description: Records admitted only after a normalisation that changed their meaning-bearing content (e.g. a formula rewritten). Must be non-zero if any such change happened.

rules.description: One entry per data-quality rule Crucible enforces, INCLUDING rules that fired zero times -- at least one entry each for: input byte budget, nesting depth, node count, string length, array length, duplicate object keys, non-finite numeric literals, timezone-naive timestamps. A rule that only appears when it fires cannot be used to prove a clean input was actually checked.

action.description: What happens when the rule fires. 'coerce' is permitted only when the coercion is lossless and recorded.

examples.description: Up to five illustrative proposal_ids. Sorted, so the artifact stays byte-stable.

quarantined.description: Every record that did not enter the pipeline, with the reason. The count MUST equal totals.records_quarantined.

locator.description: How to find the offending record in the input: a proposal_id when one could be read, otherwise a JSON Pointer such as /proposals/17.

raw_excerpt.description: A short, escaped excerpt of the offending content, truncated. MUST NOT contain unescaped control characters and MUST NOT be long enough to re-import the defect.

unit_normalizations.description: Every unit conversion applied to a claimed property, with the factor used. Unit drift between proposals is expected; silent unit drift inside Crucible is not.

sentinel_detections.description: Values that are numerically valid but are almost certainly placeholders rather than measurements.
